rationale: D1, data-informed revision of the literature-informed W0 after reading the heptane train runs. What the train data changed: the critical diameter of radiative extinction in air is 3.7 mm, not 2.8, and CO2 lowers it three times more than assumed; the hot-flame rate of a large droplet rises for 0.6 of a diffusion-clock unit while its flame develops; radiative extinction comes at 0.85 of a clock unit at the critical diameter and falls steeply above it; a cool flame follows essentially always in N2 and N2/CO2 between 15 and 21 % O2 and never with 30 % helium; the droplet keeps evaporating at 0.03-0.06 mm2/s after the cool flame. What it confirmed: the published cool-flame extinction-diameter scaling and the cool-flame rate. Numbers typed from train tables by the author; no fit, no search.
